# `edges.edges.endpoints.to`

[edges](../../README.md) · [edges](../README.md) · [endpoints](README.md) · to

an edge endpoint is a CONCEPT, never a raw view/table. It names the concept at this end; the physical relation lives in that concept's grounding plus the edge's join_rule/realized_by. Authoring an endpoint as a `view`/`key` is FORBIDDEN (additionalProperties:false rejects them): a join between stored relations that is not a join between concepts is a pipeline transform, not an ontology edge. This is what keeps edges at the semantic stage and out of the data/pipeline stage. v0.1.18: an endpoint is FULLY DEFINED or it is not an endpoint — `concept` AND `cardinality` are both required. An endpoint that names a concept and promises nothing about how many partners a row finds is half an edge: the projectors then supply the missing half themselves, silently (see `cardinality`).

### `cardinality`

*string* · **required** · 4 legal values

REQUIRED on BOTH ends — how many partners a row at the other end finds here. `1` exactly one (every key resolves AND finds at most one) · `0..1` at most one (may resolve nothing, must never find two) · `1..N` every key resolves, fan-out unbounded · `0..N` promises nothing, so nothing can contradict it. CLOSED, and the set is a MEASUREMENT of what the framework can actually judge and draw, not a taste: these four are the intersection of every live consumer's map (sdk/project/er_model.py CARDINALITY, tools/mac_to_shacl.py CARD, tools/mac_to_mermaid.py CARD_L/CARD_R, tools/check_edge_joins_measured.py EXACTLY_ONE/AT_MOST_ONE) and they are also exactly the four values the estate's edges use across all of their endpoints. WHY `1..1` AND `N` ARE REFUSED THOUGH THEY READ AS LEGAL: both are synonyms of a value already here (`1..1` = `1`, `N` = `0..N`) and both are SILENTLY MIS-RENDERED rather than rejected by a projector that meets them — mac_to_shacl defaults an unmapped value to (minCount 0, maxCount 1), so a declared `1..1` ships as `at most one`, weaker than the claim; mac_to_mermaid defaults the left terminal to `||`, so a declared `N` is DRAWN as exactly one, the opposite of the claim. Admitting a token that no judge reads and two projectors quietly rewrite is the silent-default class this requirement exists to close. `N..N` is in no consumer map, no bundle and no proposal, so it is refused outright. WIDENING THIS SET IS ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO: the pending table-link proposal (C5) adds `1..1` and `N` TOGETHER WITH the judges that would then read them; adding them here first would put the token in the grammar and leave it judged by nothing. AND THE VALUE IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CHOICE: sharpen `0..N` to `1` only with a measurement, and cite it in `verified_by`/`realized_by` rather than retyping the number.

Legal values:

- `1`
- `0..1`
- `1..N`
- `0..N`
